title: app-07: Damage-region render optimization
summary: Ottimizzazione render su scene damage-aware e scissor union.
description:
REWRITTEN 2026-11-24 after a review against main (Antonio approved). Goal unchanged: an idle or lightly animating window repaints only what changed, not the whole UI every frame (battery and heat, above all for an idle terminal).

## Current state (verified 2026-11-24 on main)
- The renderers already accept a region to repaint: `GridRenderer::set_damage` (heca-renderer/src/grid/mod.rs:301) and `TextRenderer::set_damage` (heca-renderer/src/text/mod.rs:118); `flush_scene` passes `opts.damage` to both (heca/src/app/scene_flush.rs:91-101).
- It is never used: every caller passes `damage: None` (heca/src/app/frame/mod.rs:167 `Frame::pass`, heca/src/app/frame/host_work.rs:58), and the comment at frame/mod.rs:159 says why — the scene texture is cleared every frame (`Frame::clear_and_background`, heca/src/app/frame/draw.rs:10) and panes redraw in full, so a partial repaint would leave bare background (the dark flash seen on the split button's press, 2026-06-22).
- heca-renderer/src/composite.rs keeps a persistent scene texture — the base this needs.
- Frames are already skipped when nothing asked for one (`state.needs_redraw`, frame/mod.rs:81) since T562 (idle CPU), so the win left is in frames that DO run but change a small area (cursor blink, hover glow, one pane's output).
- The old `ChromeDamageMode` was removed as unsound; do not bring it back as it was.

## Order of the work
1. T148 — stop clearing the whole scene every frame; keep the preserved scene.
2. T142 — know what changed: each pane and the chrome report the area they changed this frame.
3. T151 — clear and draw only inside the union of those areas.
4. T157 — turn it on: pass the union to `set_damage` instead of `None`; full repaint on resize, theme change, transparency change and first frame.
5. T154 — verify: no flash, no stale pixels, and a measured drop in GPU time on an idle blinking cursor.

tasks.title: Pane rendering from damage signals
tasks.description:
REWRITTEN 2026-11-24 (Antonio approved). Step 2 of P041 — read the phase description first.

Every frame must know WHICH area changed. Today the frame only knows that something asked for a redraw (`state.needs_redraw`, heca/src/app/frame/mod.rs:81). Most of the pieces already exist (verified 2026-11-24):
- Terminal panes: `client.terminal_view` returns a `TerminalDamage` with the snapshot (heca/src/app/terminal_render/mod.rs:55); it is `Full` or row ranges (heca-renderer/src/terminal/render.rs:70 `render_snapshot_damage`, :181 `dirty_rows`); viewport motion forces `Full` (heca-core/src/backend/terminal/engine/mod.rs:155).
- Widgets: the library already collects the area of every widget flagged `needs_paint` (`collect_damage`, using `Component::damage_bounds`, heca-grid-ui/src/component/behavior.rs:397; overridden by tooltip and context menu, which paint outside their bounds).

What is left: join the two into one changed area per frame (pane rows turned into window rectangles, plus the widgets' areas), in one place — not a list a new widget must remember to join. Moving or resizing anything means a full repaint.

tasks.title: Stop unconditional per-frame clear
tasks.description:
REWRITTEN 2026-11-24 (Antonio approved). Step 1 of P041 — read the phase description first.

Today `Frame::clear_and_background` (heca/src/app/frame/draw.rs:10) clears the whole scene texture every frame (transparent or opaque per config), so nothing survives from the last frame. Make the clear keep the preserved scene (heca-renderer/src/composite.rs) and clear only when the whole frame is repainted (first frame, resize, theme / transparency change) or, after T151, only inside the changed area.

Keep: transparent windows still show the frosted background in empty areas; opaque stays as today. Until T157 turns on partial repaint the full repaint must look exactly the same (no visible change).

tasks.title: Scissor union damage rect rendering
tasks.description:
REWRITTEN 2026-11-24 (Antonio approved). Step 3 of P041 — read the phase description first.

With the scene preserved (T148) and the changed areas known (T142), clear and draw only inside their union: one rectangle (the bounding box of all changed areas) is enough to start; several rectangles only if measuring shows the union is often much larger than the change. The renderers already take the area (`set_damage`, heca-renderer/src/grid/mod.rs:301 and text/mod.rs:118); the clear and the pane passes must use the same area.

tasks.title: Verify rendering with damage optimization
tasks.description:
REWRITTEN 2026-11-24 (Antonio approved). Step 5 of P041 — read the phase description first.

Verify by running, then by eye:
- Measure GPU time per frame with an idle blinking cursor and with a hover glow, before and after; report the numbers.
- No dark flash on the split button's press (the defect that removed the old attempt, 2026-06-22), no stale pixels after closing a tooltip, toast, palette or menu, after a pane scrolls, and with a transparent window.
- Antonio eye-checks the same list in the GPU app.

tasks.title: Damage gate via GridRenderer set_damage
tasks.description:
REWRITTEN 2026-11-24 (Antonio approved). Step 4 of P041 — read the phase description first.

Turn it on: `Frame::pass` (heca/src/app/frame/mod.rs:165) and host_work.rs:58 pass the frame's changed area instead of `damage: None`, and the comment at frame/mod.rs:159 is rewritten to say what is true then. A full repaint stays the rule for the first frame, a resize, a theme / transparency change, and any frame where the change is not known. One switch decides this, in one place — not a mode checked by callers (the removed `ChromeDamageMode` was that mistake).
